steps.text: Place cherries into a saucepan over medium heat. Cover and cook, stirring often, until cherries release their juices and come to a simmer, 10 to 15 minutes.
Whisk sugar with cornstarch in a bowl until combined; pour mixture into hot cherries and juice. Stir until thoroughly combined.
Bring to a simmer over low heat; cook until thickened, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool before using as pie filling.

raw_recipe.headline: Cherry Pie Filling
raw_recipe.description: This cherry pie filling recipe uses fresh or frozen red cherries to make a deliciously thick and juicy homemade filling for your favorite pie crust.
raw_recipe.name: Cherry Pie Filling

review.reviewBody: This is exactly how Grandma taught me how to make pie filling, only sometimes she'd add a tablespoon of lemon juice if the cherries turned out too sweet. This is a great recipe to take advantage of all those beautiful Washington cherries.

made this using Montmerency cherries I freeze every summer. I added 1 T fresh lemon juice and 1 tsp almond extract as well as a couple of shakes of pie spice (cinnamon, cloves, mace, ginger). II add the cornstarch , sugar and other ingredients to the juice and cook until it starts to thicken - then add cherries and turn off heat. The glaze is clear and thickens beautifully. I adjust sugar to taste. This recipe is SO EASY and ALWAYS PERFECT for pie filling or as a sauce or topping for cake, cheesecake etc. I initially made it just as written and it was delicious - just tweaked it to suit my families individual taste.

I made this exactly according to the recipe, and I rate it 4 stars as is. To make it 5 stars, add 1/2 tsp of almond extract. Then it is over the top.
I also added the sugar at the beginning of the process the last time (oops) and it turned out even better. I dumped the sugar in with the cold cherries and cooked that for about 10 minutes stirring pretty frequently. I also sifted the cornstarch to make it very fine and no lumps. Dumped in the cornstarch at the end and it thickened up in about 1 mins. 
One other helpful hint, let this cool completely before using in a pie or tart otherwise it will start to melt your crust.

As another reviewer said, make a slurry with the cornstarch first. I did not add any water, but instead used the cherry juice from the bottom of the bowl of pitted fresh cherries. So, while cherries are heating on the stove, in a bowl combine cornstarch & cherry juice, whisk until smooth. Add a few drops of almond extract. Add sugar, whisk again. Pour into bubbling pot of cherries, stirring to combine. Continue to cook, stirring frequently, until sauce has thickened. Taste a cherry and sauce for desired seeetness/ tartness. If too sweet, add a tsp of lemon juice. If too tart, add a T of sugar. Repeat as necessary. Cool filling completely before assembling pie.

After 20 years of trying to make pie filling easily, consistently delicious every time when using our hand picked frozen sour cherries, we finally found this recipe! I add a pinch or two of salt because that was what I was taught to do, but it is wonderful even when I forget. Please keep in mind it only works if you thoroughly mix the cornstarch in with the sugar before adding it to the hot cherries, otherwise you will have lumps. The beauty of this recipe is the ease of defrosting the cherries on the stove and dumping and whisking in the dry ingredients including the cornstarch. Some members of our family like cherry pie filling thickened with flour, and it works just as well, substituting 1/2 cup of flour for the 1/4 cup of cornstarch. A dash of almond extract is lovely but not necessary, and sometimes I add more sugar if my cherries are particularly tart or it’s for my sister. Highly recommend!

My 1st cherry pie made with fresh cherries from Costco. I followed the recipe but added water to the cornstarch and mixed to smooth. Added it to the cup of sugar and added a tablespoon of lemon juice to sour it a bit. Poured into a Gluten free pie crust, topped with brown sugar/butter crumble topping. Excellent!

Thank you for this starting point!
Since I had canned cherries, I had to adlib a bit.
(2) 14oz cans of cherries, 1/3 cup sugar, 2T cornstarch slurries with the drained juice from one of the cans (I saved the other juice to add to lemonade.) and 1/2t almond extract. Simmered without covering for 10 minutes.

I used canned tart cherries (15 ounce cans) and increased corn starch to 1/3 cup. I also added a little more sugar (rounded cup measure) and 1 tsp. Almond extract. It worked beautifully and was a big hit!

I used 2 cans of red tart cherries drained reserving the juice in a saucepan. Since my husband is diabetic, I used 1/2 cup stevia instead of the sugar. I also added 1/4 teaspoon almond extract after juice was thickened. Turned out great.

This is a good recipe but i substituted the sugar for agave because I'm a diabetic and regular sugar is the worst for me. Besides that, i recommend mixing the cornstarch with some cold water, before adding it to the cherries. The reason is because i added the cornstarch to my cherries and instead of blending together well, i had a lot of small lumps of cornstarch that didn't dissolve. I'll keep that in mind next time i make this recipe. Can't wait to use this for my cherry pie!

Wow so simple and delicious. Used this to make my first cherry pie ever. Notes: Used dark sweet cherries instead of tart, added 1 tablespoons lemon juice, 1/4 teaspoon almond extract, 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract. Used "Moms pie crust" (found here also at Allrecipes), baked for 55 minutes at 380.
Great recipe. But I always add a quarter teaspoon of almond extract to my filling. Adds a new dimension to the flavor... my great great grandmother's recipe from Denmark.
Perfection. I added some lemon juice and almond extract.
It's very simple.

Super easy to make! I added lemon juice and almond extract from some of the other reviewers. I also added some lemon zest. My cherries were a little on the sweet side so I only used half a cup of sugar.

So far, so good! I made this so I can freeze it in small pie size servings to have over the winter. I added a touch of almond flavoring and the taste test was spectacular! Will definitely add this to my list of pie fillings to make and freeze.
Excellent recipe. with very good instructions - it thickened beautifully. In accordance with past experience and some reviewers here, I added a 1/4 tsp almond extract and a tbsp lemon juice.

EASY EASY EASY! Pitting the cherries took longer🤣. Cooling down right now! Tastes perfect to me! These are morello cherries and will add a wee bit of almond extract, as a friend suggested. Cant wait to get it in the crust baked and sliced!!!
Great recipe! I make it with fresh or frozen cherries and it always turns out great. I add 3/4 cup of sugar and then taste for sweetness.

I made this after picking cherries from my morello cherry tree. fundamentally it works a treat, of course add additional sugar if you want it more sweet, it came out some what sharp. It would be good to have the measurements in metric the form of weight instead of volume.
